deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The bundle 'AbelTheta' and the previous page (tables of genus-3 theta characteristics written as triples like 011/011) point to Riemann's theory of the genus-3 curve as a plane quartic. That is the setting of his posthumously edited 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen fuer den Fall p=3'. This page uses the quartic in Riemann's irrational form sqrt(x y)+sqrt(z t)+sqrt(u v)=0, where x,y,z,t,u,v are linear forms (bitangents). It computes the holomorphic differential in a parametrisation by an auxiliary rational function s. A second part does an algebraic manipulation on a 'conic' relation v^2 = p^2 + q r.

(1) GENERAL LEMMA (top lines). Two relations phi(x,y,s)=0 and psi(x,y,s)=0 define a curve. Differentiating, phi_x dx + phi_y dy + phi_s ds = 0 and similarly for psi. By Cramer's rule, dx : dy : ds = J(phi,psi)/(y,s) : J/(s,x) : J/(x,y). In particular
  dx/(phi_y psi_s - phi_s psi_y) = ds/(phi_x psi_y - phi_y psi_x),
which is written correctly.

(2) THE QUARTIC. Riemann sets X = sqrt(xy)+sqrt(zt)+sqrt(uv) = 0. Here x,...,v are functions (linear forms) of two plane coordinates; confusingly, the coordinates are also called x,y, and partials are taken in y.
- The rationalised quartic is F = (xy+zt-uv)^2 - 4xyzt. It is, up to sign, the product of the four sign-conjugates of X.
- On X=0 the three conjugates other than X equal -2sqrt(uv), -2sqrt(zt), -2sqrt(xy) (my completion).
- Hence dF = -8 sqrt(xy)sqrt(zt)sqrt(uv) dX on the curve. This explains the line 'dx/(...)=dx/(8 sqrt(xy) sqrt(zt) sqrt(uv) dX/dy)'. Riemann is relating the differential dx/F_y of the rational model to dx/X_y of the irrational form; the sign -8 is suppressed.

(3) PARAMETRISATION. Riemann puts sqrt(zt) = s sqrt(xy) and sqrt(uv) = -(1+s) sqrt(xy), so that X=0 holds identically. Rationally this gives:
- phi = zt - s^2 xy = 0,
- psi = uv - (1+s)^2 xy = 0.
He notes that these imply the relation 2 s xy + xy - uv + zt = 0, which is linear in s. So s = (uv - zt - xy)/(2xy) is a rational function on the quartic.

(4) PARTIAL DERIVATIVES.
- phi_y = d(zt)/dy - s^2 d(xy)/dy
- psi_y = d(uv)/dy - (1+s)^2 d(xy)/dy
- psi_s = -2(1+s)xy = 2 sqrt(uv) sqrt(xy)
- phi_s = -2s xy = -2 sqrt(zt) sqrt(xy)
The marginal insertion '+2s(1+s)xy d(xy)/dy' records the collected cross terms in d(xy)/dy.

(5) KEY IDENTITY.
  phi_y psi_s - psi_y phi_s = 4 sqrt(uv xy zt) (d sqrt(zt)/dy + d sqrt(uv)/dy + d sqrt(xy)/dy) = 4 sqrt(xyztuv) dX/dy.
My verification:
- Using d(zt) = 2 sqrt(zt) d sqrt(zt) and 2 s^2 sqrt(xy) = 2 s sqrt(zt), we get phi_y = 2 sqrt(zt)(d sqrt(zt)/dy - s d sqrt(xy)/dy).
- Similarly psi_y = 2 sqrt(uv)(d sqrt(uv)/dy + (1+s) d sqrt(xy)/dy).
- The coefficients of d sqrt(xy)/dy combine as -s + (1+s) = 1.
Combined with (1), this yields dx/(dX/dy) = 4 sqrt(xyztuv) ds/(phi_x psi_y - phi_y psi_x). That is, the abelian differential of the quartic is expressed through ds.

(6) TOTAL DIFFERENTIALS. Riemann writes the total differentials of sqrt(zt) - s sqrt(xy) = 0 and sqrt(uv) + (1+s) sqrt(xy) = 0:
- (d sqrt(zt)/dx - s d sqrt(xy)/dx)dx + (d sqrt(zt)/dy - s d sqrt(xy)/dy)dy - sqrt(xy) ds = 0
- (d sqrt(uv)/dx + (1+s) d sqrt(xy)/dx)dx + (d sqrt(uv)/dy + (1+s) d sqrt(xy)/dy)dy + sqrt(xy) ds = 0
Both are correct. These are the irrational forms of the two linear equations in (1).

(7) SECOND COMPUTATION.
- Riemann starts from sqrt(xy) + s sqrt(zt) + p = 0 (apparently abandoned).
- He then considers v := sqrt(xy) + s sqrt(zt), a new letter, not the linear form v, so that v^2 = xy + 2s sqrt(xyzt) + s^2 zt. He writes the relation v^2 - (p + alpha q)^2 = q r. Absorbing alpha q into p, this is v^2 = p^2 + q r, equivalently (v+p)/q = r/(v-p): a conic-type (contact) representation.
- He then evaluates the function (v + p + alpha q)/(v + p + beta q). Multiplying numerator and denominator by (v - p - beta q):
  - the denominator is v^2 - (p+beta q)^2 = q(r - 2 beta p - beta^2 q);
  - the numerator is v^2 + v(alpha-beta)q - (p+alpha q)(p+beta q) = q[v(alpha-beta) + r - (alpha+beta)p - alpha beta q].
- Hence (v+p+alpha q)/(v+p+beta q) = [v(alpha-beta) + r - (alpha+beta)p - alpha beta q]/(r - 2 beta p - beta^2 q). The last line shows only the numerator after cancelling q; the denominator is unchanged.
- The purpose is presumably to write such quotients as functions that are linear in the radical v, in order to study their zeros and poles (contact conics/bitangents).

(8) RIGHT MARGIN. A faint vertical Italian note, unrelated to the mathematics (Riemann lived in Italy 1862-66): 'Ma, se ha perduto[?], deve pagare per tutto il tempo. Però andare[?], se gli piace'.
errors: Notation overload: x,y denote both two of the six linear forms and the plane coordinates with respect to which partials are taken; v later denotes sqrt(xy)+s sqrt(zt) rather than the linear form v.
In the '8 sqrt(xy)sqrt(zt)sqrt(uv)' line the factor is really -8 on X=0 (product of the three conjugate factors is -8 sqrt(xy)sqrt(zt)sqrt(uv)); sign suppressed, harmless up to normalisation.

The marginal cross-term '+2s(1+s)xy d(xy)/dy' has the opposite sign from a direct expansion of phi_y psi_s - psi_y phi_s (which gives -2s(1+s)xy d(xy)/dy). This is immaterial since Riemann proceeds via the square-root form, which is correct.
The line sqrt(xy)+s sqrt(zt)+p=0 is not consistent with the following squared relation (which defines q r rather than forcing v=-p); it appears to be an abandoned start.
Final equation shows only the numerator after cancelling q; not an error, but the denominator r-2 beta p-beta^2 q is left implicit.

results.what: Ratio formula dx/J(phi,psi)/(y,s) = ds/J(phi,psi)/(x,y) for a curve given by two equations
results.modern_name: Implicit function theorem / Jacobian (Cramer) formula for space curves

results.what: Plane quartic in the form sqrt(xy)+sqrt(zt)+sqrt(uv)=0 with linear forms (bitangents); rationalisation (xy+zt-uv)^2=4xyzt and relation between dF and dX
results.modern_name: Riemann's (Aronhold-system) normal form of the plane quartic
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures/posthumous paper on p=3, ed. Weber); H. Weber 1876

results.what: Parametrising the quartic by s = sqrt(zt)/sqrt(xy), shown rational via 2sxy+xy-uv+zt=0; expressing the holomorphic differential dx/X_y as 4 sqrt(xyztuv) ds / J(phi,psi)/(x,y)
results.modern_name: Rational function on the curve and change of variables in abelian differentials (a pencil of conics through the curve)

results.what: Identity (v+p+alpha q)/(v+p+beta q) = [v(alpha-beta)+r-(alpha+beta)p-alpha beta q]/(r-2beta p-beta^2 q) given v^2=p^2+qr
results.modern_name: Rationalising a quotient linear in a quadratic radical (contact-conic representation)

deep.surprise_reason: Scratch computations within Riemann's known theory of the genus-3 quartic sqrt(xξ)+sqrt(yη)+sqrt(zζ)=0. The algebra is correct and routine. It documents his working with an auxiliary rational parameter, but contains nothing beyond what is known from his p=3 work as edited by Weber.

transcription_corrections: Line 'dx/(dX/dy) = dx/(8 sqrt(xy)sqrt(zt)sqrt(uv) ...)': the trailing struck fragment and 'dX/dy' belong to the denominator. The line relates dx over the derivative of the rationalised quartic to dx/(8 sqrt(xy)sqrt(zt)sqrt(uv) dX/dy). The left-hand derivative is likely of the rational form, not of X itself.

The insertion '+2s(1+s)xy d(xy)/dy' is a marginal addition written to the right of the dpsi/ds line, connected by an ink stroke. It is not part of the dpsi/ds equation; the '{+ ... +}' markup is misleading.
In the second computation, 'v' is a new abbreviation for sqrt(xy)+s sqrt(zt), not the earlier linear form v.
'sqrt(xy^2)' in the denominator of the radical fraction should read sqrt(xy).

The final line ends with the numerator only, '= v(alpha-beta)+r-(alpha+beta)p-alpha beta q'; the transcription's empty denominator '{}' should be dropped. The common factor q has been cancelled and the denominator is implicit.
Right-margin Italian note: reading of 'perduto' and 'andare' uncertain; the note is faint and may be partially bleed-through.
